text: How do you run CI jobs on machines in other offices, or other countries, without opening a single port to them?
Let's say we have a controller, and three machines: one in Europe, one in the US, one in Asia. They can reach the controller. The controller can't reach them.
First, the controller creates the fleet's own certificate authority. Every machine proves who it is with a certificate from it, and checks the other side's. This is called mutual TLS.
title: MUTUAL TLS

text: Then the controller starts. It takes jobs from a GitHub organization and a GitLab runner. With no other controllers, it leads on its own.

To add a machine, we make a token. It works for one join, and expires in fifteen minutes. It also carries a hash of the fleet's authority, so a new machine can check the controller before it sends anything. This is a join token.
title: JOIN TOKEN

text: So how does a bare machine join? With one line. It downloads fleetci from the controller, checks its sum, joins with the token, and starts the worker as a service. Nothing else to install, nothing to configure.
title: ONE-LINE JOIN

text: You may ask: how does the controller know a worker can run jobs? Before it takes any, each worker boots a microVM, checks it reaches GitHub and GitLab, and saves a snapshot of it. About twenty seconds, once.
title: MICROVM CHECK

text: When the check passes, the controller marks the worker ready. Three workers, in three places, all ready.
Now, nine jobs at once: six from GitHub, three from GitLab. The leader places each job on a worker with room. The worker restores a fresh microVM from its snapshot, in two to three seconds.
title: SNAPSHOT RESTORE

text: Every job gets a VM of its own, thrown away when the job ends. Nothing carries over from one job to the next.
Now, a harder case. Let's say a microVM dies in the middle of a GitLab job.
Within seconds, the worker notices. It fails the job at once, instead of leaving it hanging, and boots a replacement, so the slot is free again.
title: DEAD VM REPLACED

text: Retry the job, and it runs on a fresh microVM, and passes.
Nine jobs. Nine passed. Three workers, anywhere.
